author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts state Sen. William Brownsberger retained the Democratic nomination in the Suffolk and Middlesex district after a two-day recount left him 35 votes ahead of challenger Daniel Lander. The hand count covered more than 24,000 ballots and changed the incumbent’s advantage by one vote from the unofficial 34-vote margin.

Brownsberger has represented the district since 2012 and serves in the state Senate’s leadership. The district includes Belmont, Watertown and portions of Boston and Cambridge. Lander, a former Boston City Hall aide, carried Boston, Watertown and the district’s Cambridge precincts, while Brownsberger’s performance in Belmont supplied the margin that preserved his lead.

Both campaigns requested recounts after the close September 1 primary. Election workers reviewed paper ballots across the four municipalities, with campaign representatives and public observers present. Lander congratulated Brownsberger after the count, and Brownsberger said he was ready to return to work for the district. The certified result moves the contest into the November general election and closes one of the narrowest Massachusetts legislative primaries of the 2026 cycle.
dek: A two-day hand count of more than 24,000 ballots changed the incumbent senator’s advantage by one vote, leaving a 35-vote margin.
headline: Brownsberger keeps Massachusetts Senate nomination by 35 votes
